transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time.
[00:04] Jillian Rowe (Peregrine - CTO): Yeah thanks Alex. We're really focused on reliability today, so thanks for coming through.
[00:10] Alex Morgan: For context I'll let Samir do a quick run on how Redwood handles fallbacks and multi-region routing but high level we support Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments and our routing and fallback policies can be tuned per-route.
[00:22] Samir Patel (Redwood SE): Yep, quick overview. We do smart routing by policy — you can prefer region, cost tier, or latency SLO. If primary capacity fails we have automatic fallback to compatible model variants or to a Dedicated pool in another region depending on your policy.
[00:34] Marco Li (Peregrine - Eng Mgr): When you say 'compatible model variants' do you mean we could fallback from a 13B quantized model to a 7B faster one?
[00:40] Samir Patel: Exactly, or to a cached response if the prefix is identical. We also support graceful degradation: shorter responses, lower sampling temp, or model downgrade.
[00:49] Priya Singh (Peregrine - SRE): How deterministic is that? Our SLAs are strict — p99 under 300ms for a lot of inference.
[00:56] Alex Morgan: Right, so tradeoffs. Hosted can hit low latencies for most workloads but if you need strict p99 we typically recommend Dedicated capacity pinned to a pool. Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and capacity isolation which helps hit hard SLOs.
[01:10] Ben Carter (Peregrine - Product): Can you do multi-region active-active routing? We have users in EU and NA and want regional failover.
[01:15] Samir Patel: Yes — we can do active-active with geo-routing and health checks. If EU primary degrades we can route to NA with automatic TTL-based routing, or you can set a preference to always serve EU but fallback to NA only on errors.
[01:28] Jillian Rowe: Any implications for data residency and logs if traffic crosses regions? We have compliance constraints.
[01:33] Alex Morgan: Good point. For Hosted we can limit data residency by region but cross-region failover would mean logs or payloads may traverse regions unless you use Private with our VPC option or Dedicated with an EMEA-only pool. For regulated workloads we often recommend Private or EMEA-only Dedicated.
[01:49] Priya Singh: What about encryption, KMS, and audit logs?
[01:52] Samir Patel: We integrate with customer KMS for Private and Dedicated. Hosted uses our managed KMS by default but we have BYOK options for enterprise accounts. Audit logs and access trails are available via the Console and can be exported to your SIEM.
[02:03] Marco Li: If we lose a region or there's an incident in the cloud provider, what's the failover time?
[02:07] Samir Patel: It depends on the policy. Health checks and BGP-like detection can detect failure in ~10-30s; routing and model warmup might add 10-30s depending on cold start. We use proactive warm pools and KV cache prewarming for hot prefixes to reduce cold start impact.
[02:20] Jillian Rowe: Those numbers matter. For our endpoint that generates conversational replies, we can't have a 60-90s blip.
[02:25] Alex Morgan: Agreed. That's where Dedicated with pre-warmed lanes and cached KV prefixes helps. Also you can configure automatic fallback to a lightweight local model as a last resort, or to a cached reply, both of which are sub-second.
[02:38] Ben Carter: Can you quantify the cost of pre-warmed capacity? Our CFO will ask.
[02:42] Alex Morgan: Sure — pre-warmed capacity is charged as reserved capacity (monthly) and depends on GPU class and number of lanes. We'll send a pricing sheet showing tradeoffs: lower per-token on sustained Dedicated commit vs higher flexibility but variable cost on Hosted.
[02:56] Marco Li: Are fallbacks always to lower quality models? We worry about user experience degrading significantly during failover.
[03:02] Samir Patel: Not always — you can setup model cascades where we try the same family with different quantizations first, then degrade response length or use a reranker. You can also use A/B style routing to test fallbacks.
[03:12] Priya Singh: How much of this is config vs something your Ops team manages? We don't want to be on-call every time.
[03:18] Alex Morgan: You control policies via the Console/ API. We provide sensible defaults and recommendations via Redwood Optimize, and our CSM/SE team can manage runbooks and hand-off for critical flows.
[03:29] Jillian Rowe: Can you walk through an incident example? Say realtime instabilities in NA region during peak.
[03:35] Samir Patel: Sure. Example sequence: monitor detects elevated p99 and error rates -> routing policy marks region unhealthy -> traffic fails over to backup region or Dedicated pool -> automatic warm cache attempts to reuse KV cache or fallback to compatible model -> if latency still fails, system returns an informative error with degrade flag and triggers alerts to your SRE and to our on-call if you opted into SLA-managed incident response.
[03:56] Marco Li: And the failover decision is per-request? per-route?
[03:59] Samir Patel: Per-route policy, and we can do per-customer overrides. So the chat endpoint can have a stricter policy than embeddings.
[04:07] Ben Carter: We use embeddings too, and those are more cost-sensitive. Could embeddings be routed differently?
[04:11] Samir Patel: Yep per-route and per-model. For embeddings you'd often prefer cheaper, quantized models in a Dedicated pool and a fallback to a lower-cost variant rather than cross-region routing that adds latency.
[04:21] Jillian Rowe: What's Redwood's SLA for Hosted? And Dedicated?
[04:25] Alex Morgan: Hosted has a published best-effort SLA for uptime; for enterprise customers we offer SLA tiers on Dedicated — typically 99.9%+ depending on the commitment and region. We'll share the SLA packs.
[04:36] Priya Singh: In an SLA event, what's the crediting process? Is it automated?
[04:40] Alex Morgan: We have automated incident logging and SLA calculation but credits are issued after validation. For Dedicated customers with contracts it's spelled out in the MSA.
[04:48] Marco Li: Any prior incidents you can share as examples? We want to understand root causes and mitigations.
[04:52] Samir Patel: Without naming customers, common incidents recently were cloud provider network blips and autoscaler storms. Mitigations included warm pools, throttled queues, and better health-check sensitivity. We also implemented model-variant fallback logic to reduce p99 spikes during autoscaling events.
[05:09] Ben Carter: Do you have any built-in chaos tests or failover drills we can run?
[05:13] Samir Patel: Yes, we can run chaos tests in a sandbox: simulate region outage, throttle capacity, verify fallback behavior. We recommend running these during POC.
[05:21] Jillian Rowe: Ok, timeline — we're targeting a pilot in Q4 and production in Q1. Security review and procurement will be gating.
[05:28] Alex Morgan: Understood. Procurement and security are typical gating items. We'll send SSO/SAML instructions, SOC2/ISO docs, and the security questionnaire.
[05:35] Priya Singh: One more question on observability: can we get token-level latency breakdowns and per-route traces?
[05:40] Samir Patel: Yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost and latency, per-route dashboards, tracing hooks and exportable logs for your observability stack.
[05:48] Marco Li: If we go Dedicated and later need to expand regions, how painful is it to add another Dedicated pool?
[05:54] Samir Patel: We can provision additional Dedicated pools; lead time depends on capacity but we have burst options and partner regions. We'll coordinate capacity planning during the committed contract.
[06:04] Ben Carter: Any gotchas around VPC peering or Private deployment networking?
[06:08] Alex Morgan: For Private, we provide a control plane with customer-managed networking. Typical gotchas are NAT/PAT rules, egress policies, and ensuring KMS endpoints are reachable. Our onboarding runbook covers those.
[06:19] Jillian Rowe: Great. Can you include a sample routing policy in the doc? We want to review fallbacks in writing.
[06:25] Samir Patel: I'll attach a sample policy and a simple YAML example for active-active geo failover.
[06:30] Priya Singh: And the bench test — we'll hand off 24 hours of traffic to Samir?
[06:33] Samir Patel: Yes please, sample traffic (anonymized) helps with kernel selection and recommended quantization. We'll also ask for p50/p95/p99 targets.
[06:40] Alex Morgan: Quick recap then. We'll send pricing and SLA docs, security pack, sample routing policy, and benchmark template. Samir will coordinate the technical deep dive and bench run.
[06:51] Jillian Rowe: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
[06:54] Ben Carter: Thanks.
[06:55] Alex Morgan: Thanks folks, we'll follow up via email.
